records.subagent_summary: My 8 rollouts scored 1/8 (exec 149.378). Every failure judged ignorance from 2002 itself, then said the holder of v can just subtract or divide, wrote impossible/contradiction (17-54 times in five rollouts), and finished on looks: 143 boxed three times, 13 once justified explicitly by primality, 14 once. Three burned the 16384-token cap. Not one rollout pooled the partners a single v admits across BOTH unstated readings into one list, so none located the residual ambiguity, and none ever exhibited two concrete legal partners for any v. The incumbent says predicate abstractly and the model echoes the word without executing it, so the revision inverts the direction: solve first for the v that WOULD know (pooled list of size one), let ignorance delete exactly those, and require two exhibited partners before calling a v ignorant - a positive check that cannot be satisfied by declaring a contradiction.

records.mutation: redirect-verification-into-reexpand-completed-square-check (with attribution rule) and replace the roots-of-unity ban clause; add no-guessed-center clause
records.subagent_summary: 8/8 correct, so training is saturated (train_i 1.0) and the only lever is transfer and wasted budget. Every rollout had the modulus ratio and the completed-square circle inside its first ~900 tokens, then spent most of the remainder on verification the incumbent already forbids: 8-40 explicit exponential root expressions each, re-deriving individual solutions to spot-check them. The worst (8378 tokens, 30 hedges, 76 'center' mentions) instead posited a center at (h,0), imposed the distance condition on that point, got two bogus centers, and oscillated ~5k tokens between them and its own correct algebra before recovering. Diagnosis: a bare prohibition leaves the checking urge nowhere legitimate to go. So the revision redirects it to a cheap portable check inside the same algebra (re-expand the completed square, r > 0) plus an attribution rule, and bans imposing the locus condition on an unproven point.

1/8 correct; wrong verdicts moved off the frame error the incumbent spends most of its tokens banning. Three failures built the wedge correctly and then declared the shapes disjoint (cover 'lies outside' S), overlap 0, answering the summed areas; one declared containment and subtracted all of area(S). The incumbent's 'P inside S kills disjointness' is a bare assertion and none of them ran it. Four other failures computed the correct clipped area and union early (4-6k chars), then reopened the rotation question and burned the whole 16384 cap (104-196 rotation mentions) without ever boxing; the lone winner reached the same value and closed. So the revision spends the freed tokens on one executable two-sided sign test that pins overlap strictly between 0 and area(S), killing both wrong verdicts at once, and orders the first computed union boxed before any angle is weighed, with congruence as the closing proof.

8/8 correct, so the skeleton is sound and the remaining cost is budget and clarity: rollouts spent 8.0k-14.4k tokens (mean ~11k) and every one detoured before the answer. Five re-litigated whether reuse forces a single function's own consecutive values to step by the common difference ('must be linear'); four called the product 'too high' and reopened tightness; and the incumbent's 'never chain adjacent terms: neighbours may differ' was repeatedly misparsed as 'each term must use a different polynomial' (9, 9, 18 hits in three rollouts), forcing a rebuild of the setup. So the prohibition is read as a constraint on assignment rather than on inference. This revision states the positive rule the model kept rederiving - the constraint is purely pointwise, P(n)=T(n), and a source may repeat - which makes neighbour-differencing vacuous without a ban, adds cap-one-class-then-sum to block reporting N, and separates a construction's size from the bound.

records.mutation: ban-parameter-as-log-base and treat negative-discriminant/absurd-identity as an inverted-factor signal, with numeric calibration from the given pair
records.subagent_summary: 6/8 correct; both failures hit the 16384-token cap after the closure equation came out with the argument factor inverted, and neither ever reached the root test the incumbent relies on because there was no real root to test. One rollout wrote log U = log V - 1 when its own two lines gave log V = log U - 1, i.e. it added dy to the wrong vertex, and got discriminant -92. The other substituted the function's parameter letter b as the LOG BASE in the log-difference identity, producing a bogus factor, roots outside the domain, then a diagonal-midpoint detour that forced Q onto M. Correct rollouts instead exponentiated each point alone and read the factor with the printed base. So the revision bans using an argument parameter as the base, calibrates the factor from the given pair which already realizes (dx,dy), and converts negative-discriminant or absurd-constant-identity into one reciprocal flip instead of endless re-derivation.

0/8; the graded quantity is the last sub-answer and every rollout missed it. All 8 explicitly wrote that the shed's bottom bag is the one carried LAST, then read the answer off a uniform model: 1/4 from 'each bag equally likely to be moved last' (idx 0,1,2,3,4,5,7), or 0 after declaring the order always reversed (idx 6). Part a came from templates: 1/2^(n-1) (idx 0,1,2,5), 1/24 (idx 4,7), 1/256 (idx 3). Not one rollout wrote a concrete move order with per-step legality. So the incumbent's declarative arrival-rank rule keeps losing to the flip. This revision makes orientation decide WHICH END of the run to analyse: last carried answers about the top, so a bottom or k-th-from-bottom question is about the earliest arrivals and is settled from the opening moves. Forced/free 1/2 pricing and the run-of-halves warning are kept.

records.mutation: ratio-irregularity-as-arithmetic-error-detector (replace back-substitution check with a cross-case consistency test that catches a mis-solved small case before any law is fitted)
records.subagent_summary: 0/8. Diagnosis: the ladder ran, but a single corrupted small case poisoned every fit. Six rollouts reached 3+ sizes, yet not one produced a clean value set. One built the smallest case with equal instead of one-fewer zero conditions, got a spurious value, then spent ~9k tokens forcing signed-factorial, power, and (n-1)!-type laws onto that inconsistent triple before hitting the cap. Another got a different corrupted smallest value, fit a clean power-of-2 law to it, and shipped it confidently. Two others abandoned numbers for full-size product/coefficient expansion (55-142 coefficient-of-x mentions). The incumbent asks for back-substitution, but rollouts never do it (0 hits). So this revision replaces the ignored per-case check with a cheap cross-case test the model already gravitates to: consecutive ratios plus signs must be regular, and irregularity means re-solve a case rather than invent a law.

7/8 rollouts correct. All eight derive the common divisors and the maximal candidate correctly, so the divisor core works; the loss is entirely in reading management. The failure (longest, 15.5k tokens, 40 backtracks, 6 self-declared contradictions) adopted a reading where each listed aggregate was simultaneously a per-unit amount, which forces the count to cancel to a nonsense value; it then spent most of its length looping on that dead branch, and once exhausted it accepted both surviving candidates as valid and picked the smaller one, the group count, as the 'most reasonable' story. Winners never entered that branch. Rounds 14-18 tried tie-break bans and substitute-back checks after the fact and lost heldout, so instead of policing the endgame I added an up-front screen: a reading in which N cancels, is forced to 1, or aggregates double as per-unit amounts is self-refuting and gets dropped, not explored. That kills the branch that produces the bad tie.

7/8 correct (3.5k-5.4k tokens); the one failure burned the full 16384-token cap and ended in a degenerate loop repeating one subtraction hundreds of times. It adopted the centered ansatz, then mis-nested the composition (substituting the already-cubed offset again, BA^9, so B^2=A^8, B=+-A^4, 16 mentions). Fatally, it then eliminated in the wrong direction: it solved each given for the scale, A=(r+24)/r^3 and B=(r-30)/r^3, and pushed those into the branch relation, producing (r-30)^2*r^14=(r+24)^8, then trial-substituted integer centers. All 7 correct rollouts imposed the branch relation on the givens first and added the pair, closing in one line. Rounds 9/10 (exponent audits), 14/15 (factoring), 16 (no-ratio), 17 (validate) and 18 (conjugation) all lost heldout, so this revision changes only the elimination order and adds a portable back-up trigger: a high-degree equation in one unknown means wrong order, not a root hunt.

records.mutation: block-swap-j-to-j+L-offset-rule + cross-size grow-and-divide consistency filter that blames the larger trace
records.subagent_summary: 3/8 correct; 3 of 5 failures hit the 16384-token cap. Mechanical root cause: three rollouts collapsed a length-L block swap into a single-slot transposition (writing 'swap 0-1, swap 0-2, swap 0-4'), so idx6 got n disjoint 2-cycles and boxed 2, idx5 invented a 6-cycle+2-cycle and boxed 2n. idx1 built a position table where the length-2 swap moved slot 1 back to 1; it contradicted its own state trace and it burned 16k tokens re-arguing instead of trusting the states. Fit-stage cause: every failure held per-size counts that did not grow (idx7 traced 4 for size 4 then a botched 4 for size 8; idx2 listed 4,4,8), then fit an off-by-one exponent or went piecewise/special-case rather than redoing the larger trace. So the revision adds the explicit j <-> j+L slot rule, a two-repeat order-2 falsifier, and a cross-size filter (counts grow, smaller divides larger, bounded by slot count) that blames the LARGER trace.
